description: Team Wyrd is a student team from Islamabad, Pakistan, competing in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are computer science and data science students who love turning open data into answers people can actually use. Our skills span Python, machine learning, data analysis and visualization, and we work best as a team — each of us bringing a different strength to the same problem. "Wyrd" is Old English for destiny — we build the future, we don't wait for it.
summary:
Dust ended two NASA Mars missions: it buried InSight's solar panels in 2022, and a planet-wide storm silenced Opportunity in 2018. Dust Twins finds where on Earth dust behaves like it does at a Mars landing site, and in which months, so dust-sensitive hardware can be tested there first.

We compared 13 Mars years of orbital dust maps with 24 years of NASA MERRA-2 Earth dust records, giving every place on both planets the same fingerprint: the shape of its dust year, how stormy it is, how hazy, and how much it swings year to year. For each of five landing sites, the app shows ten Earth twins and a month-by-month test calendar, and every result is checked against scrambled seasons and the rovers' own sky readings. None of the famous analog sites keeps a Mars dust year.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Dust Twins is an interactive web app. Pick a Mars landing site (InSight, Opportunity, Spirit, Perseverance or Curiosity) and Earth lights up with the ten places whose dust behaves most like that site's. Each twin comes with a test calendar: the Earth months that line up with the dustiest stretch of the Martian year. Examples: InSight's site matches Bechar, Algeria (score 0.89, test May to August); Opportunity matches Vihari, Pakistan (0.88, April to July); Spirit matches Diplo, Sindh, Pakistan (0.88, March to June).

HOW IT WORKS

Every place on both planets gets the same four-number fingerprint, built on 12 seasonal bins a year: the shape of its dust year, how often months run stormy, its haze rank on its own planet, and its year-to-year swing. All four are ratios or ranks, so Mars infrared and Earth visible measurements can be compared fairly. Earth's year is then turned month by month until its shape fits the Mars site; the best turn sets the calendar.

WE PUBLISH THE CHECKS, INCLUDING WEAK ONES

- Shuffled baseline: at every site, all ten top twins beat matches made with scrambled months.

- Rover ground truth: the orbital Mars record agrees with dust measured by the rovers themselves (InSight r = 0.94, Opportunity 0.79, Spirit 0.97).

- Storm-year detector: with no list to go on, it finds Mars's three global dust storms (2001, 2007, 2018).

- Famous analog sites: Atacama, Iceland, Hawaii and Antarctica do not keep a Mars dust year under this method.

- Weak, and shown as weak: odd and even years agree only moderately (0.56 to 0.75), and we did not register expectations before the run.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Mars dust hardware (solar panels, cleaning systems, sensors) is mostly tested in lab chambers. Dust Twins points engineers to real field sites and the right months for those tests, on reachable ground in Africa and South Asia rather than only the usual analogs. Every card says plainly what Earth can never copy: thin air, low gravity, static-charged dust.

CREATIVITY

Two SI features run inside the app. "Argue against this twin": a model reads only the pipeline's figures and gives the strongest reasons the match could fail; every number it cites is checked against the data, and unverifiable claims are dropped. "Ask a planning question": a model looks up the answer step by step and turns the globes to it. A narrated 30-second story mode walks through the InSight case.

TOOLS

Data pipeline: Python (xarray, NumPy, SciPy, netCDF4, earthaccess, Pillow). App: Next.js, React, TypeScript, three.js / react-three-fiber, Tailwind CSS, hosted on Vercel. SI: Claude (code), Google Gemini (in-app features), ElevenLabs (narration). Videos: Playwright and ffmpeg.

Code and full method: https://github.com/Salman-Labs/dust-twins
